newsitem.title: USA: Dry soils, good potential for NW Kansas wheat - tour.
newsitem.headline: Dry soils, good potential for NW Kansas wheat - tour.

text.p: Crop scouts saw dry soil in fields toured in northwest Kansas on Tuesday but crop prospects were average to above average, Wheat Quality Council tour participants said.
"A rain on this would do wonders. It's dry about four inches below the surface," said a grain company wheat marketing specialist who declined to be named.
Yield potentials in Phillips, Smith and Norton counties ranged from roughly 40 to 50 bushels per acre, crop scouts said after touring 15 fields in northern Kansas.
Phillips County was the best surveyed across the northern tier, the scouts said.
Soil in Norton, Decatur and Rawlins counties in northwest Kansas was drier than in counties toured earlier in the north east and north central parts of the state, participants said.

Yield potentials in Decatur and Rawlins ranged from 35 to 40 bushels per acre. Last year, which was an extremely dry year for western Kansas wheat, fields in Norton and Decatur yielded a meager 20 bushels per acre while Phillips County produced 29 bushels per acre.
Wheat fields surveyed in northwest Kansas were virtually disease-free although a small amount of wheat streak mosaic, a fungus that causes yellowing of the leaves, was detected.
The crop was in the "flag", or head-in-boot development stage, the final stage of stem extension before heading.
